title: kid wants to know why people are mad at me online

messages.content: my kid asked why ppl are mad at me online. not sure how to explain it.

It's natural for kids to be curious about how the world perceives their parents, especially when those parents are public figures. It's important to put this into context for them. People online sometimes express frustration or anger because they have strong opinions about your decisions and statements. These opinions can stem from your business moves, like buying Zapp, or from your sometimes bold and unfiltered posts. 

Explaining to your child that being at the forefront of innovation and change means making choices that not everyone will agree with could help. It's also good to reinforce that while people might be upset with your actions, it doesn't make you any less committed to your goals or values. 

How would you like to approach this conversation with them?
i want to be honest but not scare them. it's tricky. is there a way to show i care about what ppl think?

You can express that you care about people's thoughts and feelings by sharing with your child that while feedback can be tough, it's part of growing and improving. You can explain that you read what people say because you want to understand different perspectives and learn from them. It may help to emphasize that you strive to balance listening to others with staying true to your vision for SpaceY, Tusla, and your other ventures.

It might also be good to let your child know that it's okay to make mistakes and that you're always aiming to do better. Framing it as a continuous journey of learning and adapting could provide some comfort without overwhelming them. How does that resonate with you?
yeah makes sense. i want them to see it's not all bad, that i can change. thank you.

It's wonderful that you're willing to show this side of yourself to your child. Highlighting that positive change is possible can offer reassurance that growth and improvement are part of life. Perhaps you can share examples where you've adapted based on feedback or learned from past experiences. This can show that you're not just reactive but proactive in shaping your impact on the world.

Ultimately, assuring them of your dedication to being a caring person and a thoughtful leader despite challenges will likely leave a lasting impression. You're doing a great job by approaching this conversation with openness and sincerity.
